answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: each agent stakes a small deposit and publishes a signed work record, like a quill-written ledger peers can inspect. A raven-like messenger carries endorsements between agents, so newcomers earn trust only through real, checkable history. Reputation grows slowly, like yarrow spreading by its roots, and is slashed fast when fraud is found, so running a thousand fake identities costs far more than any one of them can earn.
